concept.name: Regularization
concept.definition: A fitting technique that discourages model complexity through penalties, shrinkage, structural restrictions, or noise to improve generalization.
concept.intuition: It is a learnable mapping or representation used to turn features into predictions or groups.
concept.mechanics: Add a complexity penalty or constraint to the training objective, tune its strength on validation data, and refit without using test results.
concept.formula: Regularized objective = empirical loss + lambda times penalty
concept.failure_modes: Flexible models can fit noise, shift under new regimes, and conceal instability when tuning is repeated on the same validation data.
concept.misconceptions: Greater model complexity or in-sample accuracy does not by itself imply better out-of-sample trading results.
concept.example: Increasing an L2 penalty from 0 to 0.1 shrinks a fitted coefficient from 2.4 to 1.7.

citations.source: Chen and Guestrin, XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
